scope: Durable events, SSE reconnect/replay, cursors, truncation and missed/duplicate transitions; store/http (src/store.ts, src/http.ts, Coordinator.waitForStateChange, GET /events, get_worker_logs pagination, redactor as used by the event path, runtime event log flush).

findings.title: GET /events re-parses the entire worker table once per string field, stalling the single-threaded event loop
findings.evidence: src/security.ts:43-50 redactorFor() returns a Redactor whose `secrets` is a thunk that calls c.store.all() (SELECT body FROM workers + JSON.parse of every row, each row embedding a prompt of up to 32000 chars per src/domain.ts:33). src/security.ts:7 Redactor.text() invokes this.secrets() on EVERY call, and Redactor.value() recurses into every string field. src/http.ts:45 calls redactor.value(e) for up to 100 events per request, each with 3 string fields (worker_id, type, data) => 300 full table scans + 300 full JSON parses per request. The redactorFor() call at src/http.ts:42 looks like per-request construction but is lazy and snapshots nothing.
findings.reproduction: Bun 1.4.2, local fakes, tmpdir SQLite, no network (probe /tmp/rv13/probe/repro.ts). Production defaults: SWARMFORGE_MAX_WORKERS=50, prompts at the 32000-char schema maximum => 1634620 bytes of worker bodies, 100 events. Result: 'GET /events x3 = 1588ms (529ms per request, single-threaded)'; 'same query WITHOUT the redactor = 0ms'; 'store.all() calls caused by redacting one 100-event page = 300'. Scaling with a full 100-event page: N=25 -> 133ms, N=50 -> 786ms, N=100 -> 2001ms, N=200 -> 4225ms (linear in retained workers x page size). An empty page costs 0-1ms, so cost is entirely per-delivered-event. 6s of reconnect-polling at 50 workers/32000B prompts consumed 5704ms of event loop (951% of one core), because the SSE 'retry: 2000' directive makes a browser EventSource poll this endpoint continuously. Consequence: Bun runs the server on one thread, so this stalls all MCP calls, the coordinator tick (SWARMFORGE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=2000) and /health; SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN is optional (src/config.ts:81).
findings.recommendation: Resolve the secret list once per request instead of per call: in redactorFor, compute the array eagerly and close over the array (or memoize the thunk with a per-request scope). Optionally redact the serialized JSON string once per event rather than walking each field, and add an events(worker_id, id) index (see the companion missing-index note in the MEDIUM finding).
findings.confidence: high - reproduced deterministically; the 300 store.all() calls per 100-event page is an exact count, and the linear scaling was measured across four worker counts

findings.title: wait_for_state_change ignores its own deadline while draining a large event backlog
findings.evidence: next() (src/coordinator.ts:119-135) loops lifecycleEvents(cursor, filter, 200) until it matches or exhausts the table. The deadline is checked only AFTER next() returns, at src/coordinator.ts:141 and :160. With a non-matching `states` filter or a stale cursor, the scan runs to the end of the table regardless of timeout_ms. The events table has no retention (docs/OBSERVABILITY.md:30 makes pruning an operator responsibility) and no index at all (PRAGMA index_list(events) returns []), so the drain grows without bound over server lifetime. metrics.ts:102/113/125 additionally run three unindexed `WHERE worker_id=?` scans plus a temp B-tree group-by per worker per scrape on the same unindexed table.
findings.reproduction: Bun 1.4.2, local fakes (probe /tmp/rv13/probe/drain.ts), single worker, synthetic backlog, call = waitForStateChange({worker_id, cursor:0, states:['destroyed']}, {timeoutMs:0}): 100000 events -> 74ms, 400000 -> 289ms, 1600000 -> 1200ms. timeout_ms=0 is documented as 'checks once' (src/mcp.ts:296, docs/MCP-API.md:23) but performs a full-table drain. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN confirms the scan is a rowid range walk with no worker_id index.
findings.recommendation: Pass the deadline into next() and break out of the batch loop when Date.now() >= deadline, returning the consumed cursor so next_cursor stays accurate. Separately add CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_worker_id ON events(worker_id, id) to fix the same missing-index problem on the metrics surface.
findings.confidence: high for the mechanism and the unbounded-growth property (deterministic, EXPLAIN-confirmed); the 1.6M-event figure is a synthetic upper bound rather than a measured production backlog, so real-world severity depends on how large the operator's events table grows

tests.command: bun test tests/wait.test.ts tests/http.test.ts tests/api.test.ts tests/restart.test.ts
tests.summary: Exit 0; 22 pass, 0 fail, 114 expect() calls across 4 files, using official Bun 1.4.2 at /tmp/rv13/bun142/bun-linux-x64/bun (snapshot Bun 1.3.14 cannot read lockfileVersion 2; lockfile not modified). bun install --frozen-lockfile into the /tmp clone. Full suite intentionally not run (whole-suite reviewer's scope). Targeted behaviour was additionally verified with 24 disclosed local probes under /tmp/rv13/probe using only FakeProvider/FakeAgent and :memory:/tmpdir SQLite; no real provider, VM, model endpoint or cloud call.

limitations: Timings come from a single shared-CPU container; absolute milliseconds will differ, but the linear scaling in retained workers x page size and the exact 300 store.all() per page count are deterministic. Finding 1's worst case assumes maximum-size prompts; with 200-byte prompts at 50 workers the cost drops to 57ms/request but remains linear. Finding 2's severity depends on the real size of the operator's events table. The missing-index metrics claim rests on EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN plus a 200k-event render (15ms), not a realistic long-lived backlog. No concurrency test of the waiter against a busy coordinator tick was run. Verified-correct and deliberately not reported: SSE replay is exact under truncation (301 events paged via Last-Event-ID gave 301/301 delivered, 0 duplicates, 0 missing, strictly increasing); cursor validation rejects abc/-1/1.5/>2^53; next_cursor on timeout prevents cross-filter event skips; transition() is idempotent per state; listener lifecycle returns listenerCount to 0 on every exit path; /events is a finite 200 (server closes in ~2ms) which matches the documented bounded-replay model; event payloads carry no prompt.
